intro: These three look alike but split into two ideas. を問わず ("without asking about X") and にかかわらず ("not depending on X") both cover every possible value of X: the result is the same whichever way X goes. にもかかわらず adds も and is different in kind: X is one real fact, and something happened in spite of it. First question every time: is X a range of possibilities, or one fact that is true?

skills.rule: Category noun + を問わず: X is not a condition; anyone or anything, whatever its X, is included ("regardless of", "no matter").
skills.explain:
問う means "to ask about, to make an issue of", so 年齢を問わず is literally "not asking about age". It follows a noun that sorts people or things into kinds: 年齢, 性別, 国籍, 経験, 学歴, 季節, or a paired noun that covers both ends: 男女, 昼夜, 内外, 晴雨, 有無 (経験の有無を問わず, with or without experience). The second half is usually inclusive: anyone can apply, it is popular with everyone, it is open all year.

It is typical of notices, job adverts and descriptions. It attaches to nouns, including noun pairs with か (有料か無料かを問わず). After verbs and adjectives, use にかかわらず: 参加するしないにかかわらず, 行くかどうかにかかわらず.

Do not confuse it with に限らず, "not only X": 子どもに限らず大人も (not only children but adults too). に限らず widens from one named case to others; を問わず says the category does not matter at all.
patterns: [年齢 / 性別 / 国籍 / 経験] を問わず [anyone can / popular / accepted]
[paired noun: 男女 / 昼夜 / 内外] を問わず

examples.jp: 年齢[ねんれい]{を問[と]わず}、だれでも参加[さんか]できます。
examples.en: Anyone can take part, regardless of age.

examples.jp: この歌手[かしゅ]は男女[だんじょ]{を問[と]わず}人気[にんき]がある。
examples.en: This singer is popular with men and women alike.

examples.jp: 駅前[えきまえ]の道[みち]は昼夜[ちゅうや]{を問[と]わず}混[こ]んでいる。
examples.en: The road in front of the station is busy day and night.

examples.jp: ここは季節[きせつ]{を問[と]わず}楽[たの]しめる場所[ばしょ]です。
examples.en: This is a place you can enjoy in any season.

examples.jp: 経験[けいけん]の有無[うむ]{を問[と]わず}、スタッフを募集[ぼしゅう]しています。
examples.en: We are recruiting staff, with or without experience.

examples.jp: 国籍[こくせき]{を問[と]わず}、留学生[りゅうがくせい]を受[う]け入[い]れています。
examples.en: We accept international students of any nationality.

contrast.note: Often interchangeable after nouns (年齢を問わず / 年齢にかかわらず). After verbs and adjectives (行く行かない, 行くかどうか) use にかかわらず; を問わず stays with nouns.
にもかかわらず means "despite" one actual fact: 雨にもかかわらず (although it was raining). を問わず never refers to a single fact.
に限らず means "not limited to X" and is followed by も: 日本に限らず、海外でも人気がある (popular not only in Japan but abroad too).

mistakes.bad: 子[こ]ども{を問[と]わず}、大人[おとな]も楽[たの]しめる。
mistakes.good: 子[こ]ども{に限[かぎ]らず}、大人[おとな]も楽[たの]しめる。
mistakes.note: "Not only children but adults too" widens from one case: に限らず, not を問わず.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]{を問[と]わず}、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]われた。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]{にもかかわらず}、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]われた。
mistakes.note: The rain was one fact that really happened, so it is "despite": にもかかわらず. を問わず needs a range of values.

skills.tip: Picture a sign: "Age, gender, experience: not asked." If X is a category that could be written on a form, を問わず fits.

skills.rule: X with several possible values + にかかわらず: the result is the same whichever value X turns out to have ("regardless of", "whether or not").
skills.explain:
かかわる means "to be connected with, to depend on". にかかわらず says the result is not tied to X. X must be something open, with more than one possible outcome: a noun such as 天候, 結果, 年齢, 金額, 経験の有無; a pair of opposites such as 行く行かない, 好き嫌い, 多い少ない; or a question clause with かどうか or a question word (行くかどうか, 何を選ぶか).

The clause after it states something fixed: an event goes ahead, a rule applies, a request stands. It is neutral to formal and very common in announcements.

The classic error is mixing it up with にもかかわらず. にかかわらず covers all cases before they are known; にもかかわらず reacts to one fact that is already true. 天候にかかわらず実施します means "held rain or shine"; 雨にもかかわらず実施した means "held despite the rain (that fell)".
patterns: [noun with options] にかかわらず [fixed result]
[clause] かどうかにかかわらず

examples.jp: 天候[てんこう]{にかかわらず}、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]われます。
examples.en: The match will be held whatever the weather.

examples.jp: 結果[けっか]{にかかわらず}、必[かなら]ず連絡[れんらく]します。
examples.en: We will contact you whatever the result.

examples.jp: 好[す]き嫌[きら]い{にかかわらず}、野菜[やさい]も食[た]べなさい。
examples.en: Whether you like them or not, eat your vegetables too.

examples.jp: 参加[さんか]するしない{にかかわらず}、返事[へんじ]をください。
examples.en: Please reply whether or not you will take part.

examples.jp: 買[か]うかどうか{にかかわらず}、試着[しちゃく]はご自由[じゆう]にどうぞ。
examples.en: Feel free to try things on, whether or not you buy.

contrast.note: にもかかわらず follows one fact that is true and introduces a surprising result: 熱があったにもかかわらず出勤した (went to work despite having a fever).
を問わず is limited to nouns, mostly categories of people and things. にかかわらず also takes verb and adjective pairs and verb clauses with かどうか.
に応じて is the opposite idea: the result changes to match X. 年齢に応じて料金が違う (the fee depends on age) vs 年齢にかかわらず料金は同じ (the same fee at any age).

mistakes.bad: 熱[ねつ]があった{にかかわらず}、会社[かいしゃ]に行[い]った。
mistakes.good: 熱[ねつ]があった{にもかかわらず}、会社[かいしゃ]に行[い]った。
mistakes.note: Having a fever is one fact that was true, so it is "despite": にもかかわらず.

mistakes.bad: 年齢[ねんれい]{にかかわらず}料金[りょうきん]が違[ちが]います。
mistakes.good: 年齢[ねんれい]{に応[おう]じて}料金[りょうきん]が違[ちが]います。
mistakes.note: If the result changes with X, it does not stand regardless of X: use に応じて (or によって).

skills.tip: Can you add "...or not" or "whatever it turns out to be"? Then にかかわらず. If X already happened, it is にもかかわらず.

skills.rule: Fact + にもかかわらず + unexpected result: "in spite of X", "even though X".
skills.explain:
にもかかわらず takes a fact that is true and reports a result that goes against what that fact would lead you to expect: 雨にもかかわらず人が集まった (people came despite the rain). The も is the "even" that marks the surprise.

It attaches to nouns (雨にもかかわらず, or 休日であるにもかかわらず), plain verbs (注意したにもかかわらず), plain い-adjectives (高いにもかかわらず), and な-adjectives with である or だった (静かであるにもかかわらず). It can also open a sentence on its own: にもかかわらず、彼は来なかった.

It is formal and objective. Like のに, the second half cannot be a request, order, invitation or intention: for "come even if it rains" use 雨でも来てください. のに is the everyday version and carries the speaker's frustration; it can even end a sentence (せっかく来たのに). ものの concedes a point and then reports that things went no further: 買ったものの、使っていない.
patterns: [noun] (である) にもかかわらず [unexpected result]
[plain verb / い-adjective] にもかかわらず
[な-adjective] である / だった にもかかわらず

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]{にもかかわらず}、たくさんの人[ひと]が来[き]た。
examples.en: Despite the rain, a lot of people came.

examples.jp: 値段[ねだん]が高[たか]い{にもかかわらず}、よく売[う]れている。
examples.en: Even though it is expensive, it is selling well.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは熱[ねつ]があった{にもかかわらず}、会社[かいしゃ]に来[き]た。
examples.en: Mr. Tanaka came to the office despite having a fever.

examples.jp: 何度[なんど]も注意[ちゅうい]した{にもかかわらず}、同[おな]じミスが続[つづ]いている。
examples.en: In spite of repeated warnings, the same mistake keeps happening.

examples.jp: お忙[いそが]しい{にもかかわらず}、お越[こ]しいただきありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for coming despite being so busy.

examples.jp: 休日[きゅうじつ]である{にもかかわらず}、店[みせ]は空[す]いていた。
examples.en: Even though it was a holiday, the shop was quiet.

contrast.note: Without も it means "regardless of" and covers every possible value: 天候にかかわらず (rain or shine). にもかかわらず reacts to one fact that is true.
のに is conversational and emotional (disappointment, complaint) and can end a sentence. にもかかわらず is formal and neutral, for writing, news and polite speech.
ものの grants the first point and says the follow-through fell short: 習ったものの、もう忘れた. It does not follow a bare noun; にもかかわらず does.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]{にもかかわらず}、来[き]てください。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]{でも}、来[き]てください。
mistakes.note: No requests, orders or intentions after にもかかわらず; use でも or ても.

mistakes.bad: 部屋[へや]は静[しず]かな{にもかかわらず}、眠[ねむ]れなかった。
mistakes.good: 部屋[へや]は静[しず]かだった{にもかかわらず}、眠[ねむ]れなかった。
mistakes.note: な-adjectives connect through である or だった, not な.

skills.tip: Is X a fact that is already true, and is the result a surprise? Say "despite" in English: if it fits, にもかかわらず.
